entityDescription:
Planetek Hellas, a member of the D-Orbit Group, is a leading Greek company active in Earth Observation, geospatial intelligence, and software development for both satellites in orbit and their ground systems.
Founded in Athens in 2006, the company combines deep expertise in satellite data exploitation, geoinformation systems, and participation in major ESA and European Commission programmes.
The company’s expertise covers a wide spectrum of activities, including:
- Ground Segment systems for mission control and satellite operations
- Mission planning, control, and AI-powered payload data ground systems
- In-orbit software and AI-based onboard processing (AI-eXpress)
- Spatial Data Infrastructures (SDI) and Copernicus-based applications
- Advanced Earth Observation services for environmental monitoring, civil protection, defence, and security

The company operates its own Satellite Command and Control Centre (C2) in Kifisia, Athens – a modern infrastructure serving as a national hub for satellite mission operations that supports both civilian and defence applications.
Through continuous innovation, research, and talent development, Planetek Hellas has become one of the most dynamic players in Greece’s and Europe’s space ecosystem, committed to turning satellite technology into operational value for society, government, and strategic autonomy. Planetek Hellas provides solution oriented services in the field of Geomatics, involving the use of EO data and systems for environmental & critical infrastructure monitoring, urban planning, civil protection and security.

entityName: University of Osijek Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences Osijek
description:
The mission of the Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences Osijek is aimed at sustainable development obtained via high-quality and effective education based on the modern learning outcomes and the concept of lifelong learning, as well as on the training of highly qualified experts. Scientific activity is founded on the development and dissemination of basic, applied, and developmental research in order to obtain new knowledge and ideas through critical thinking and creativity. The Faculty enables the students to acquire competencies based on modern scientific knowledge by virtue of knowledge and technology transfer and by an active cooperation with the economic entities and community-based developmental partners. The Faculty promotes the development of the economy and of a wider social community by involving them in the European Research Area (ERA) and the European Area of ??Higher Education (EAHE). 
As one of the leading research and higher educational institutions in the field of biotechnical sciences in the region, the Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences Osijek will develop a research and educational profile recognized on the international level. By 2025, the Faculty will become recognizable in the biotechnical and interdisciplinary scientific fields of research, in which it will achieve excellence on the international level, actively participate in the European Research Area (ERA), and profile itself as a biotechnical center of excellence for the transfer of knowledge and technologies to the economy.
entityDescription: Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences Osijek is part of the Josip Juraj Strossmayer University of Osijek and is one of its oldest members. 18 October 2015 marked exactly 55 years of its foundation. Besides teaching students at undergraduate, graduate and postgraduate studies, the major activity of the Faculty is scientific research, primarily in the field of Agriculture and Biotechnology. Scientific and teaching faculty have the task of educating students, gradually introducing them into the world of basic knowledge about plants, animals and farming technologies so that they could independently manage processes of agricultural production, whose ultimate goal is production of food for human community. In this complex process of education, teachers use their own knowledge of scientific and professional work, and thereby enhance and modernize the education of students. Alongside with the education of students, research assistants together with professors and professional staff are engaged in research in the fields of biology, chemistry, nutrition and protection, genetics of plants and animals, engineering and economics in crop and livestock production, all with the aim of qualitatively and quantitatively improving food production and at the same time reducing production costs and conserving nature, environment and human health.

description:
EmTDLab is a deep-tech materials company using proprietary AI to develop next-generation radiation shielding for satellites, space assets, and critical infrastructure, creating advanced materials that enhance protection and performance: 
- We are powered by SYMADE.AI, an AI-driven systematic material discovery engine that serves both as our internal innovation core and as a service enabling partners to expand their materials knowledge and accelerate innovation.
- We design, synthesize, and manufacture novel materials that are lighter, more cost-effective, and highly efficient for radiation shielding applications.
- The European Space Agency has officially verified and validated our proprietary software and materials platform, confirming its technical maturity and unlocking commercial pathways and strategic growth opportunities.
entityDescription:
EMTDLAB stands for “Emerging Technologies Development Laboratory”
Core business of the company
Discover, develop and manufacture materials for high-performance space radiation shielding combined with high structural performance. Market the materials to aerospace companies, space agencies, space electronics manufacturers, aerospace engineers and system integrators. Create leadership in this niche market based on novel, proprietary Materials Informatics methods and high-throughput manufacturing.
EmTDLab technology value proposition is the use of Materials Informatics (M.I.) to perform systematic search for materials composition with optimal radiation shielding and mechanical properties. 

Target Market Segments
Early Stage: (1) Commercial-of-the-shelf electronics component manufacturers willing to access the New Space market using EmTDLab technology to smart shield component at chip- and board-level; (2) Substitute radiation-hardened, radiation tolerant and fault-tolerant / fault-detection systems with external radiation shields; (3) Contract Research Services for radiation simulation and spacecraft optimisation;
Later Stage: (1) Larger surfaces of new materials types will be manufactured for entire spacecraft’s: satellite walls, spaceship pressure hull, spaceship debris and radiation shield; (2) Aerospace engineering services outsourcing;

Application Range – Commercial Use Cases
Both structural materials for living organism’s on-board spacecraft / space vehicles & shielding materials for space electronics: satellites, robotic probes, launch vehicles, crew exploration vehicles, landers & ascent vehicles, rovers, mining robots, astronauts suits, planetary power systems; building materials for planter system.

Physical & Chemical Properties Optimisation
· Radiation Shielding
o High Energy Protons
o High Energy Electrons
o Galactic Cosmic Rays (Heavy Ions)
o Secondary neutrons
o Optional : Gamma Rays and EMI
· Thermal Management
o Heat Dissipation / Heat Sink
· ATOX – Atomic Oxygen Corrosion
 
Mechanical Properties Optimisation
· Specific Strength
· Specific Modulus
· Fracture Toughness
· Fatigue Crack
 
Application Range – Commercial Use Cases
Both structural materials for living organism’s on-board spacecraft / space vehicles & shielding materials for space electronics:
· Satellites
· Robotic probes
· Launch vehicles
· Crew Exploration Vehicles
· Landers & ascent vehicles: planetary & asteroids
· Planetary rovers: manned and automated
· EVA suits
· Photovoltaic panels (planetary power systems)

entityDescription:
Satellite communication has essentially contributed to today’s most advanced society through data transmission, mobile telephony and television. An alternative and addition to all terrestrial communication systems, therefore providing a lot of potential for future trends. For example, ideas such as Industry 4.0, the Internet of Things (IoT) or autonomous driving require powerful communication networks, which are capable of reaching every location worldwide.

To demonstrate and to bring these capabilities into focus, the German Center for Satellite-Communications r.S. (DeSK) was founded in 2008, unifying enterprises, scientific institutions and universities, operating in the field of satellite communication.

DeSK’s objective is to promote the expansion of business relations among the members to create a powerful network, capable of initiatingsynergies.

In addition, the institution organizes workshops to find qualified and trained professionals. The association also initiates a dialog with relevant stakeholders from political sectors and the industry with the goal to incorporate the versatile possibilities communication satellites provide, into political infrastructure plans and other economic sectors.

Further, DeSK operates an interactive showroom to demonstrate the relevance of satellite communication technology in our daily lives. With the slogan “Touch and Feel Satellite Communication" the showroom informs the general public as well as young talents about new trends and topics in this field.

entityDescription:
HUN-REN Centre for Energy Research (HUN-REN EK) is an organisational unit of a newly established Hungarian Research Network, operating as a distinct legal entity with its own legal personality. As of 28 October 2025, the budgetary-institution status of the HUN-REN Centre for Energy Research (EU VAT No.: HU15327040) ceased, and from 29 October 2025, the Centre continues to operate as an organisational unit of HUN-REN Hungarian Research Network. The newly established HUN-REN Centre for Energy Research (EU VAT No.: HU19426196 ) is the general legal successor of the former budgetary institution regarding rights and obligations.
HUN-REN EK comprises three research institutes: the Institute for Atomic Energy Research, the Institute for Energy Security and Environmental Safety, and the Institute for Technical Physics and Materials Science. The mission of the research centre is to perform research and development in the field of nuclear science and technology for facilitating the adoption and the safe use of nuclear technology in Hungary, to participate in international research efforts aiming at the establishing a new generation of nuclear power plants and closing the fuel cycle, to study the interaction of radiation (including neutrons, gamma-rays and electrons) with matter, and to do isotope and nuclear chemistry, chemical analysis by nuclear methods, radiography, radiation chemistry, radiation protection and nuclear security, surface chemistry and renewable energy research. In the field of technical physics and materials science, research efforts are concentrated in the following topics: the interdisciplinary research on complex functional materials and nanometer-scale structures, exploration of physical, chemical, and biological principles, their exploitation in integrated micro- and nanosystems, and in the development of characterization techniques. HUN-REN EK provides technical support for the Nuclear Power Plant Paks as well as the Hungarian authorities. The Institute operates the 10 MW Budapest Research Reactor (BRR), providing the scientific community of Europe (Budapest Neutron Centre) with research possibility for neutron physics and its applications, and supplying Hungary with radioactive isotopes, mainly used by medical applications. HUN-REN EK, as developer of several space radiation and space dosimetry systems, is one of the founding members of the Hungarian Aerospace Technology Platform (HATP).

description:
Vesper AS (Norway) – Patented Engineering Concepts for High-Speed & Space Systems 
Vesper AS is a technology transfer and IP venture company. We originate high-impact engineering concepts, protect them through patent filings, and commercialise via licensing, joint development programmes, and JV/SPV structures with capable industrial partners. 
Opportunity: FALAK – Adaptive Hypersonic Heat-Management System FALAK is a lightweight, adaptive thermal-management concept for vehicles exposed to extreme aerodynamic heating, including high-Mach atmospheric flight and re-entry. Traditional thermal protection is typically sized for worst-case peak heating, adding mass, cost, and refurbishment burden. FALAK is designed to manage heat flux in real time where and when it matters most—reducing reliance on conservative overdesign. 
What it addresses :
- Highly non-uniform, time-varying thermal loads 
- Migrating hotspots driven by trajectory, dynamic pressure and surface conditions 
- Thermal bottlenecks that constrain vehicle architecture and performance 
Target benefits:
- Reduced thermal protection and structural mass through lower peak design margins 
- Improved component lifetime and system reliability under transient heating 
- Better reusability potential and shorter refurbishment/turnaround cycles 
- Increased design flexibility for next-generation high-speed and re-entry platforms 
Status & IP:
- Early development stage (approx. TRL 2–3) 
- IP being protected through patent applications filed by Vesper AS 
- Technical specifics, integration interfaces and performance targets are shared under NDA 
Partner we want (co-financing & execution capability): 
We are seeking industrial partners and research organisations able and willing to co-finance and execute a staged validation pathway, such as: 
- Thermal analysis and modelling capability (CFD/FEA/heat transfer) 
- High-enthalpy / high-temperature test capability (e.g., wind tunnel, arc-jet or equivalent) 
- Materials, TPS, high-temperature structures and integration competence 
- Access to relevant programmes and funding channels for demonstrator work 
Collaboration formats: 
Funded feasibility studies, joint demonstrators, licensing, or structured joint ventures—depending on partner needs and programme constraints. 
If you work on reusable launch systems, re-entry vehicles, or high-speed flight demonstrators where thermal margins drive mass and cost, we welcome a confidential dialogue to assess fit and define a validation plan.
entityDescription:
Vesper is an early-stage startup focusing on thermal management for hypersonic vehicles. 
By developing concepts that reduce heat-loads at extreme velocities, we aim to enable safer, more efficient platforms for the space industry.

Falak is our first development project. 
Falak brings real-time, adaptive thermal control to hypersonic flight and re-entry—actively targeting localized hotspots as thermal profiles shift. 
By reducing peak heat loads where they matter most, Falak cuts thermal-protection mass to improve speed and reduce weight, while strengthening survivability under extreme aerodynamic loads. 
The result is a pathway to higher reusability of aerospace components and faster, more repeatable mission cycles.

description:
Gorilla IT develops high-quality applications with measurable impact. As a high-tech innovation company, operating at the intersection of model-driven development and semantic interoperability, we provide organizations with an integrated approach to managing the complexity of modern digital ecosystems and effectively using their information assets.
Gorilla IT is a European leader in Model-Driven Development (MDD), with expertise in transforming conceptual models into secure, compliant, maintainable, and future-proof IT solutions. Our methodology is grounded in Fact-Based Modelling, and we have decades of experience converting conceptual models into operational software artifacts, including databases, web services, and full-stack applications.
We maintain a strong global network within the Fact-Based Modelling community, working closely with tool vendors and academic institutions. Gorilla IT has actively contributed to the European Space Agency’s (ESA) vision of semantic interoperability. Based on our expertise in the ORM language and tools such as NORMA Pro, ESA selected us to develop the first version of the Space System Ontology (SSO), in collaboration with Airbus Space & Defence, OHB Systems, Thales Alenia Space, and ArianeGroup. Our contributions continue through multiple initiatives. We have supported the formalization of the ORM metamodel (FAMOUS-2) and assisted ESA in transforming academic research on ORM into practical, globally accepted formats, including hierarchical structures, class diagrams, and other conceptual representations. We also worked with large system integrators to extend the SSO to additional domains. 
Currently, Gorilla IT is extending its expertise to the field of artificial intelligence by linking semantic models with AI and reasoning capabilities. Our track record includes the delivery of high-quality solutions for organizations in sectors such as finance (e.g., ABN Amro, Achmea, Centraal Beheer) and energy (e.g., Shell). These projects illustrate our capacity to deliver solutions that remain relevant and effective over time.

entityDescription:
The Desertification Research Centre (CIDE) is a public scientific research centre. Due to our nature as a mixed centre, three institutions are involved in our management: Spanish Research Council (CSIC), theUniversity of Valenciaand theAutonomous Government of Valenciathrough theConselleria de Agricultura, Desarrollo Rural, Emergencia Climática y Transición Ecológicaand theConselleria de Innovación, Universidades, Ciencia y Sociedad Digital.
At CIDE we work, since its origin, to provide knowledge based on scientific evidence, and to communicate to society the importance of environmental issues, and in particular, about the risk and potential impact of desertification and climate change on ecosystems and human beings, and thus contribute to the protection of our environment. In this sense, we are one of the pioneer centers in Europe in the study of desertification and one of the few institutes devoted to this topic, with a solid base and extensive experience in the study of soil, water and ecosystem degradation processes, mainly in the Mediterranean. In constant evolution, our strategic objectives, included in our Action Plans, are aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
To carry out our work, we have a multidisciplinary team with 17 researchers on staff whose lines of work are framed in the Departments of Environmental Quality and Soils, and Ecology and Global Change; and we have a total of 88 workers including administrative and service staff, technicians and researchers and pre and postdoctoral researchers.
From a more applied point of view, many of the studies we carry out have implications for the management of nutrients and water in agricultural systems, and in a more general framework for land management, biodiversity conservation and ecological restoration.
CIDE has participated and participates in multiple research and environmental advisory committees at regional, national and international levels. The Centre participated in the elaboration, development and monitoring of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification, including Annex IV of the Regional Implementation for the Mediterranean; and in regional and national desertification control plans, such as the National Action Program to Combat Desertification (PAND). It also advises the Valencian Parliament, Generalitat Valenciana (Advisory and Participation Council for the Environment (CAPMA), Forestry Board, Threatened Flora Committee, etc.), European Parliament, OECD, the Joint Research Centre (JRC), UICN, etc.
This centre also contributes to academic and professional training through its participation in different masters and doctorate programs of different universities (Univ. Valencia, Univ. Politécnica de Valencia, Univ. de Alcalá de Henares, etc.), as well as collaborating in the training of university personnel through the supervised internship programs of the different universities.

entityDescription:
Datafuchs Oy is a Finnish AI company building geospatial intelligence software for organisations that depend on spatial data to make decisions. 
 
The company's flagship platform, Geofuchs, replaces manual GIS analysis workflows with AI agents that understand natural language. Where a GIS analyst might spend days processing satellite imagery, correlating layers, and producing a report, Geofuchs completes the same analysis in minutes — querying hundreds of authoritative data sources, reasoning over spatial relationships, and returning interactive map visualisations directly from plain-language requests.
 
The platform is built for the European public sector and regulated industries: municipalities, national mapping agencies, infrastructure operators, and forestry and agriculture enterprises. These are environments where data sovereignty, auditability, and integration with official EU/national data standards are non-negotiable. Geofuchs is designed from the ground up for that context — natively compliant with EU INSPIRE mandates and sourcing data from authoritative national providers.

Datafuchs was founded by a team combining enterprise software delivery experience across Fortune 500 clients with deep Nordic market knowledge. The company is headquartered in Finland.

entityDescription: Ascilient is building Water-as-a-Service commercial infrastructure for municipal wastewater and industrial water reuse, starting in Denmark and scaling across Europe to help accelerate solutions to a growing global water crisis. We use a data-driven diagnostic approach—including satellite imagery and other external datasets—to quantify needs, constraints, and outcomes, then translate that into measurable, output-based requirements and a standardized contractual foundation. This reduces friction in procurement and deployment by making projects comparable, performance-auditable, and easier to tender and finance. The result is faster adoption of advanced treatment and recirculation solutions with clearer risk allocation and more predictable delivery.
